The '''Voidfire Nebula''' was in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Voidfire Nebula was first mentioned in the roleplaying magazine article "[[Crystal Web Space Station: A Setting for the Star Wars: New Republic Campaign|Crystal Web Space Station: A Setting for the ''Star Wars: New Republic'' Campaign]]", which was published without [[Lucas Licensing]] approval and thus is considered non-canon.<ref name="Unlicensed">{{UnlicensedStatus}}</ref> However, it was later included in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', canonizing its existence and placing it in the Expansion Region.

===Non-canon content===
The nebula was an ionized [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] that stretched across a vast region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], covering as much space as a medium-sized [[Star system/Legends|star system]]. It was located at the junction of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] and two other [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] (one providing a pathway from one edge of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] to the other, and the other connecting the [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] systems to the neutral worlds of the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]), as well as being near [[Crystal Web Station]]. The [[Lucent]]s claimed that their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] was located somewhere in the nebula, which could account for their peculiar [[Crystal/Legends|crystalline]] technology.

This [[Cosmic storm/Legends|cosmic storm]] crackled with charged particles and explosions of color. Even at a distance, the nebula threw off so much static and energy that [[Starship/Legends|ship]] [[Computer/Legends|computers]] and electronic systems could suffer ion damage just by being close to it. All [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump points within the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] fell within the area of the nebula. As soon as a ship actually entered the nebula, they took constant ion damage. Because Lucent technology was based on crystals and gems rather than traditional means, they could traverse the nebula without suffering from these effects.

[[File:Voidfire_Nebula.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Crystal Web Station and a [[Crystal Star Tug]] on the edge of the Voidfire Nebula]]

Another effect of the nebula was that the charged energy emanating from it wreaked havoc on navigations systems and [[Navigation computer/Legends|strogation computers]]. Because of this, even though [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogators]] had long ago calculated the benefits of this region of space as far as hyperspace travel was concerned, few [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] if any were brave enough or good enough to chance making a jump through this natural [[Interdiction field/Legends|interdiction field]]. When the Crystal Web Station appeared sometime between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] survey of [[8 BBY/Legends|8 BBY]] and [[Daran Tal]]'s scout ship accident in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the benefits of the area's hyperspace jump points suddenly became accessible to all space travelers for whatever price the Lucents charged.
